Anthropic published the chart itself. On Frontier-Bench v0.1, the agentic terminal coding evaluation that Claude Opus 5 leads by an embarrassing margin, the model peaks at the xhigh effort level and then comes down slightly at max. The headline figure Anthropic reports is 43.3 percent; the peak on the curve sits a fraction above it. The same shape appears on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, where the score drops at max while the cost per task keeps climbing.
That is a strange thing for a vendor to put in a launch post, and it is the most useful thing in the entire release.
Most of the coverage since Friday has been about price. Opus 5 costs five dollars per million input tokens and twenty-five per million output, unchanged from Opus 4.8, and Anthropic is positioning it as roughly Fable 5 intelligence at half of Fable 5 rates. Fine. That story will be rewritten forty more times this week. The part that will actually change what you type into a configuration file is the effort parameter, and specifically the fact that its top setting is not the best setting.
